theme: पाप और प्रसंग / Sin, consequence, and the moral weight of violence
context: The moral logic deepens. Arjuna no longer asks only whether the kill is justified; he asks what the emotional and spiritual aftertaste of that act would be. Even if the adversaries are enemies, the act of killing them would bring guilt and moral corrosion.
contextHindi: मूल सवाल अब सिर्फ ‘कौन सही है?’ नहीं रहा; अर्जुन पूछ रहे हैं कि इस हत्या का मन पर क्या असर होगा। अगर उनके शत्रु भी हैं, तब भी उनके वध से हृदय में पाप, ग्लानि और नैतिक पतन का भाव उठेगा।
sanskritDevanagari:
निहत्य धार्तराष्ट्रान्नः का प्रीतिः स्याज्जनार्दन |
पापमेवाश्रयेदस्मान्हत्वैतानाततायिनः ||१-३६||
transliteration:
nihatya dhārtarāṣṭrānnaḥ kā prītiḥ syājjanārdana .
pāpamevāśrayedasmānhatvaitānātatāyinaḥ ||1-36||

wordByWord.meaning: the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra; the Kauravas, the relatives before him
what pleasure; what joy or satisfaction

sin, moral stain, the burden of harm done
would cling to; would accrue to

spokenHindi:
अर्जुन यहाँ सीधे-सीधे कहते हैं—'इन धृतराष्ट्र-पुत्रों को मारकर हमें कैसी प्रीति होगी, जनार्दन? अगर हम इन आततायियों को मार भी दें, तो इसके बदले हमारे ऊपर पाप का ही बोझ रहेगा।' यह बात बहुत गहरी है। अक्सर हम सोचते हैं कि ‘शत्रु को मार दिया, तो समाधान हो गया।' लेकिन अर्जुन की दृष्टि कहती है कि कर्तव्य का सवाल सिर्फ बाहरी परिणाम नहीं है; उसका भीतर भी एक नैतिक असर होता है।

शत्रुता हो, अपराध हो, हिंसा हो—ये सब वास्तविक हैं; पर उसी परिस्थिति में भी मन की शुद्धि और आचार की रक्षा का सवाल उठता है। अर्जुन अपने भीतर से पूछते हैं कि अगर इस हत्या से हमें संतोष है, तो वह संतोष सही है या केवल एक मानसिक बहाना है? बहुत बार हम ‘उचित कारण’ के नाम पर आत्मा को दबा देते हैं, लेकिन वह काला धब्बा भीतर ही भीतर रह जाता है।
clearEnglish:
This verse shifts from the question of personal reluctance to the question of moral consequence. Arjuna asks not only whether the enemy is deserving of death, but whether victory would leave the victors spiritually wounded. The point is not that the opponents are innocent in every way; it is that the act of killing them would still bring a burden of sin, guilt, and moral contamination to those who do it.

The verse is therefore not a blanket statement about all violence, but a warning about the shadow cast by violence on the doer. A person may justify an act as necessary, but if the act damages the soul’s clarity, then the apparent success becomes tainted. This is why the Gita often asks us to look beneath the immediate tactical logic and examine the deeper effect on character, conscience, and responsibility.

interpretationPerspectives.label: Text
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The verse states directly that killing the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra would not bring joy but would generate sin, even if the act is framed as necessary or justified.

interpretationPerspectives.label: Commentary
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The DLS edition reads this as the moral burden of violence, not as a simplistic condemnation of war. The corpus transliteration is preserved exactly here, including the precise spelling `dhārtarāṣṭrānnaḥ` and `janārdana`.

interpretationPerspectives.label: Inference
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: A sober inference is that strategic necessity does not cancel the ethical residue of violence; a person can still be morally harmed by choosing the act they think is unavoidable.

practicalApplication.label: Check the inner cost
practicalApplication.text: When a difficult action seems necessary, ask what burden it leaves in your conscience, relationships, and sense of integrity—not only what it gains in the moment.

practicalApplication.label: Separate justice from self-corruption
practicalApplication.text: A just cause can still become corrupting if the means snuff out empathy, restraint, and inner balance; choose means that do not hollow the self.

reflectionQuestion: What action in my life feels justified on the outside but leaves a hidden moral weight inside me?
reflectionQuestionHindi: मेरे जीवन में कौन-सा काम बाहर से सही लगता है, लेकिन अंदर एक छिपी हुई नैतिक भार छोड़ जाता है?
